correctness.rationale: The source Fourier identity is uniform in its real phase parameter. For arbitrary fixed beta, auxiliary poles remain within a fixed distance 1+|beta| of integer labels, exceptional integer-residue conditions remain finite per index pair, and nonresonance gives pairwise distinct poles and uniform discreteness. The weighted summability, ergodic pole-density bound, and Jensen zero-density contradiction therefore persist.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant arXiv:2609.20805 retains |beta|<1/2 even in its stronger nonresonant one-dimensional specialization. Searches by source identifier, exact frequency formula, nonresonance condition, and quasicrystal/universal-completeness terminology found no amplitude-free equivalent. Residual risk remains because the source is extremely recent.

value.rationale: The theorem removes the amplitude restriction entirely in dimension one, covering every nonzero rational beta and all but countably many real beta for each fixed irrational alpha, while preserving universal L1 uniqueness and Lp completeness for all measurable spectra of measure below one.
